brief.summary: Acoustic analysis software for independent bat ecologists and environmental consultants who sort ultrasonic recordings from survey detectors into species identifications for client reports.
brief.user: Dr. Ines Marchetti, a self-employed bat ecologist who does pre-construction surveys for wind farms and developers. She is an expert on bat calls but switched to this software two days ago after her old program stopped receiving updates.
brief.moment: She has imported three nights of recordings from a wind-farm site and is going through the program's first-run walkthrough, but she is stuck. The automatic classifier labeled 41% of files as noise, far more than she's used to, and she suspects a sensitivity setting or a detector sample-rate mismatch. She needs to understand what the program's terms mean compared to her old software, find out why so many files were thrown out, and learn how to manually check the calls before she bills the client for an interim report due next Wednesday.
brief.data: Project 'Hollins Ridge Wind — Pre-construction, Autumn 2026', client Ridgeline Renewables. 3 detectors (HR-01 meteorological tower at 50 m, HR-02 forest edge, HR-03 pond), nights Nov 9–11. 2,814 recordings (WAV, 256 kHz and 384 kHz, 3–15 s). Classifier results: 1,154 noise, 812 Myotis spp., 403 Eastern red bat, 227 hoary bat, 141 big brown/silver-haired group, 77 unclassified. Noise share by detector: HR-01 18%, HR-02 39%, HR-03 66% (likely insect noise at the pond). Settings include minimum call frequency 15 kHz, signal threshold 18 dB, minimum calls per sequence 3, and the regional classifier pack 'Eastern US v4.2'. Onboarding progress: 4 of 9 steps done. Help covers 60 topics, including 'Noise filter vs. classifier confidence' and 'Importing from other detectors'.

prompt:
I need the front end for Echolog. Acoustic analysis software for independent bat ecologists and environmental consultants who sort ultrasonic recordings from survey detectors into species identifications for client reports.

Who's using it: Dr. Ines Marchetti, a self-employed bat ecologist who does pre-construction surveys for wind farms and developers. She is an expert on bat calls but switched to this software two days ago after her old program stopped receiving updates.

What they're doing right now: She has imported three nights of recordings from a wind-farm site and is going through the program's first-run walkthrough, but she is stuck. The automatic classifier labeled 41% of files as noise, far more than she's used to, and she suspects a sensitivity setting or a detector sample-rate mismatch. She needs to understand what the program's terms mean compared to her old software, find out why so many files were thrown out, and learn how to manually check the calls before she bills the client for an interim report due next Wednesday.

What's in the system at this point: Project 'Hollins Ridge Wind — Pre-construction, Autumn 2026', client Ridgeline Renewables. 3 detectors (HR-01 meteorological tower at 50 m, HR-02 forest edge, HR-03 pond), nights Nov 9–11. 2,814 recordings (WAV, 256 kHz and 384 kHz, 3–15 s). Classifier results: 1,154 noise, 812 Myotis spp., 403 Eastern red bat, 227 hoary bat, 141 big brown/silver-haired group, 77 unclassified. Noise share by detector: HR-01 18%, HR-02 39%, HR-03 66% (likely insect noise at the pond). Settings include minimum call frequency 15 kHz, signal threshold 18 dB, minimum calls per sequence 3, and the regional classifier pack 'Eastern US v4.2'. Onboarding progress: 4 of 9 steps done. Help covers 60 topics, including 'Noise filter vs. classifier confidence' and 'Importing from other detectors'.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
